benchmark.title: VectorForge reports faster search
benchmark.article: VectorForge says its new index cut median query latency from 40ms to 20ms on one million 768-dimensional vectors, using one client on a 64GB machine. Recall stayed at 95%. The index used 48GB, up from 24GB. The team has released the benchmark script but has not tested concurrent clients. The release is a prototype.

pricing.title: LedgerCloud changes its pricing
pricing.article: LedgerCloud will replace its $20 monthly developer plan with a $5 base fee plus $1 per thousand API calls on November 1. The company says 60% of current accounts make fewer than 10,000 calls a month. Existing annual contracts keep their price until renewal. Usage alerts arrive at 80% of a customer-set budget; they do not stop requests. Customers can set a hard cap, which rejects excess requests.

The central tension is whether a 20ms latency cut justifies doubling index memory and whether it holds outside the single-client benchmark.

- Doubling RAM from 24GB to 48GB can raise hosting costs and reduce how many indexes fit on a machine at a fixed memory budget.
- The latency reduction may suit an interactive single-user search tool, but a shared service still needs a concurrent load test.
